answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps agent interactions onto a graph, enforcing topological cut verifications across clusters. Randomly selected multi-agent auditing committees inspect bottlenecks, requiring participants to lock bonded stake. When a cut fails verification, dishonest nodes suffer stake slashing, imposing superlinear attacker cost. Honest validators like ridge nodes, opal arbiters, and cedar verifiers coordinate game-theoretic audits to penalize colluding identities.
